messages.author: df1e8c4ee64c5304
messages.subject: default priors and half-Cauchy
parts:
Probably a dumb question from a newish STAN user.

Somewhere in what I have read recently, Gelman suggested trying a half-Cauchy prior on tau in the 8schools model.  The model code installed with rstan (in R) does not set a prior for tau, and I think that this means that a default prior of [0 - infinity] is assumed.  (Correct??)  Gelman's suggestion is that one should use the half-Cauchy by adding the line:

tau ~ cauchy(0, 25);

I have tried adding this line to the parameters section, immediately after declaration of tau, and this led to a syntax error from stanc pointing to the start of the new line.  So I tried adding it instead to the model section.  Again, I got the same syntax error from stanc.

What am I doing wrong?

Larry Hunsicker

messages.author: df1e8c4ee64c5304
messages.subject: Re: default priors and half-Cauchy
parts:
[Very red face]  My apologies.
I re-typed  the "tau ~ cauchy(0, 25);" line in the model section, and this time it ran fine.  I went back to recheck what I had entered before, and even with a "microscope" I couldn't find a difference.  I suspect that there must have been a non-printing character somewhere.  
In any case, I now understand that this line has to be in the model section, as correctly stated by Mike.  And I am reminding myself that I should always simply reenter a line that looks as though it should work, but stubbornly doesn't.  
Now on to look at what difference the new prior for tau made.
